MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Medical Center
Department of Medical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Name: [redacted name]
DOB: [redacted date]
MRN: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Peripheral blood
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]

REFERRING PHYSICIAN
Dr. [redacted name]
[redacted location] Medical Associates

CLINICAL INDICATION
Carrier testing for Tay-Sachs disease

TEST PERFORMED
Targeted DNA sequencing for common HEXA variants

METHODOLOGY
Genomic DNA was extracted from peripheral blood leukocytes. Targeted sequencing was performed for the following variants in the HEXA gene (NM_000520.6):
- c.1274_1277dupTATC (p.Tyr427fs) - Ashkenazi Jewish founder mutation
- c.1421+1G>C - Ashkenazi Jewish founder mutation  
- c.805G>A (p.Gly269Ser) - Ashkenazi Jewish founder mutation
- c.739C>T (p.Arg247Trp) - Common UK variant
- Pseudo-deficiency variant screening

Sequencing was performed using Sanger sequencing methodology with bidirectional analysis. All variants are described according to Human Genome Variation Society (HGVS) nomenclature guidelines.

RESULTS

HEXA Gene Analysis:
No pathogenic sequence variants detected

Variants Tested:
- c.1274_1277dupTATC (p.Tyr427fs): Not detected
- c.1421+1G>C: Not detected
- c.805G>A (p.Gly269Ser): Not detected
- c.739C>T (p.Arg247Trp): Not detected
- Pseudo-deficiency variant: Not detected

INTERPRETATION
No pathogenic variants were identified in the HEXA gene for the common mutations tested. This result indicates that the patient is not a carrier of the most common Tay-Sachs disease mutations, including the three Ashkenazi Jewish founder mutations that account for approximately 98% of carriers in the Ashkenazi Jewish population, and the common UK variant.

RISK ASSESSMENT
Based on these results, the patient's carrier risk for Tay-Sachs disease is reduced to approximately 1 in 520. This residual risk reflects the possibility of rare pathogenic variants not covered by this targeted analysis.

RECOMMENDATIONS
The current testing has analyzed the most common pathogenic variants in HEXA. If further risk reduction is desired, comprehensive HEXA gene sequencing of all coding regions and splice sites is available. This expanded testing would detect rare variants not included in the current panel.

Genetic counseling is recommended to discuss these results, residual risk, and testing options for family members if indicated.

TECHNICAL NOTES
This test detects approximately 98% of Tay-Sachs disease carriers in the Ashkenazi Jewish population and 95% of carriers in the general population. The analytical sensitivity and specificity of this assay are >99%.

Variant nomenclature follows HGVS guidelines using HEXA reference sequence NM_000520.6.

REFERENCES
1. Kaback M, et al. Tay-Sachs disease--carrier screening, prenatal diagnosis, and the molecular era. JAMA. 1993;270(19):2307-15.
2. Myerowitz R, Costigan FC. The major defect in Ashkenazi Jews with Tay-Sachs disease is an insertion in the gene for the alpha-chain of beta-hexosaminidase. J Biol Chem. 1988;263(35):18587-9.

This test was developed and its performance characteristics determined by [redacted location] Medical Center Molecular Genetics Laboratory. It has not been cleared or approved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director
